clue.text: Female arts graduate backing the learner

indicators.note: backing means standing behind in support, so the graduate's letters come after the others

parts.note: taken as written
L is the learner, as on a learner driver's L-plate
an MA is a Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A woman with an arts degree supports the novice in her charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' puts MA behind THE L rather than reversing anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so it stands for any woman bearing that name.

clue.text: Girl in early race — that's the girl?

parts.note: a heat is a preliminary race that sorts runners before the final
her is the pronoun for the girl

explanation.surface: Pointing out a young woman running in a qualifying round: is that her?
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, also a moorland plant, standing for any girl so called.

clue.text: Entertaining match?

definitions.meaning: ... entertainment is easy, undemanding fare, so entertaining in that undemanding way
asking for a ... means asking for a match or flame for a cigarette

explanation.surface: Is this an enjoyable game of sport?
explanation.definitionFit: Light comedy is easy-going amusement, and a match is something that gives a flame.

clue.text: A spot in which you'll see navy chaps dressing up

indicators.note: the sailors are seen inside the spot, so their letters sit within it

parts.note: a dot is a small spot
RN is the Royal Navy
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Somewhere sailors can be seen putting on their finery.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamentation or decoration; the act of dressing up something to make it attractive.

clue.text: Greedy pig, not very good, harsh

indicators.note: not says the pious letters are taken away from the animal's name

parts.note: taken as written
PI is short for pious, very good in a religious sense
a rasping voice is harsh and grating

explanation.surface: A gluttonous pig, far from virtuous, with a grating squeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greedy pig' reads as one phrase; only 'Greedy' defines. 'not' strips PI (pious) from PIG to leave G.
explanation.definitionFit: Grasping people are avaricious, always clutching at more money or possessions.

clue.text: Terrible greed that consumes an important person

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so the shuffled word takes the short word inside it
terrible suggests the letters of the next word are in a bad, disordered state

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Awful greed devours someone of high standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' makes GRDEE (from greed), and 'that consumes' puts AN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandee is a high-ranking nobleman, originally Spanish, so a person of eminence.

clue.text: A Greek character proved ultimately to be a pest

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the word proved

explanation.surface: A figure in a Greek story ends up being a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person in a play; it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly and blackfly are sap-sucking insects that gardeners count as pests.

clue.text: Everyone housed in home, one with a name and in classical style

indicators.note: being housed in a dwelling means being inside it

parts.note: pad is slang for one's home
everyone means all
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Every family member lives at home, one having a title and a classical taste in design.
explanation.definitionFit: Architecture following Andrea Palladio, the Venetian architect who revived classical Roman forms.

clue.text: Against upsetting performance in part of church service

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting tips the word over so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a turn is a performer's act on stage

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a disruptive act during worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' looks like an adjective describing the performance, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocturns are divisions of the night office of Matins in the monastic liturgy.

clue.text: High-church type acting, affected with alcohol

indicators.note: affected here means altered, so the letters of both words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ritual-loving churchgoer behaves pretentiously when drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Church of England's high, Catholic-leaning wing are known by this name.

clue.text: Lost colour, with need to be changed

indicators.note: the letters of the two words need to be changed, that is rearranged

explanation.surface: Something faded and had to be replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming paler or whiter is losing one's colour, as a face does from shock.

clue.text: Make connection with mug at Oxford?

parts.note: mug and dial are both slang for the face
a student at university is said to be up, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: Getting linked up with a fool at the university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mug' suggests a fool or a cup; it is slang for a face.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring a number on a telephone, or connect to the internet over a phone line.

clue.text: Men wanting a not-half clever person to give advice

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: not-half is read as only half, so the first three of the six letters of clever

explanation.surface: Soldiers short of someone moderately bright to counsel them.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle was a source of prophecy, so now anyone consulted as an infallible adviser.

clue.text: Official order given to young lady in vehicle

indicators.note: the order and the young lady are placed inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
OM is the Order of Merit
miss is a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A girl in a car receives an honour or an instruction from a functionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A Soviet Communist Party official, especially one in charge of political education.

clue.text: What could be mooniest feelings

indicators.note: these words say the answer is what a rearrangement of the next word could be

explanation.surface: Sentiments that are dreamiest of all, as if moonstruck.
explanation.definitionFit: Feelings and emotions are synonyms for states such as joy, grief or love.

clue.text: Fixer of musical instrument is getting particular note right

parts.note: an organ is a keyboard instrument
E is one of the musical notes

explanation.surface: A repairer of an instrument tunes one note correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixer of musical instrument' reads as a repairer; only 'Fixer' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An organiser arranges and fixes things, like events or meetings, so a fixer.

clue.text: Weapon something frightening almost? I'm having it locked up

indicators.note: locked up means shut inside, so these letters go within the trimmed word
almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: something frightening is scary
taken without its apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone holds a fearsome blade under lock and key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims SCARY to SCAR, and 'locked up' puts IMIT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved, single-edged sword associated with the Middle East and Central Asia.

clue.text: The first person to turn up in Irish town, someone from the distant past?

indicators.note: the reversed pronoun is placed inside the town name

parts.note: Cavan is a county town in the Republic of Ireland

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: me is the first person pronoun

explanation.surface: Wondering about the first person to arrive in an Irish town, perhaps an ancient settler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The first person' suggests Adam; it is the grammatical first person, ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A prehistoric human who lived in caves, so a person of the remote past.

clue.text: Once again deal with hiding place

definitions.meaning: to treat again, to handle a second time

explanation.surface: Revisiting a secret bolt-hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-treat it means handle again; as one word it is a place of seclusion.

clue.text: Pleasant information I presented to US gangster?

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: Nice details passed to an American mobster.
explanation.definitionFit: A genial person is friendly and cheerful, so pleasant company.

clue.text: A gang operating in ditch

parts.note: a band is a group or gang of people
something operating is on, working

explanation.surface: A crew of workmen busy in a trench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditch' looks like a trench to dig; it is the verb meaning to give up.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch something is to discard or desert it altogether.

clue.text: Keeps away from keen son, concealing love

indicators.note: concealing means hiding something within, so love's letter goes inside

parts.note: avid means keen
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: An eager boy hides his affection and keeps his distance.
explanation.definitionFit: To shun or steer clear of someone or something.

clue.text: Dawn gets boy out of bed, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the answer sounds like the spoken phrase

parts.note: a son is a boy; someone out of bed is up

explanation.surface: Early morning, and the lad is getting out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunrise, the moment the sun appears, is the start of the day.

clue.text: New unit established by Welsh woman in African city?

indicators.note: the woman's name follows to complete the word
new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters of unit

parts.note: Sian is a Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: A Welsh woman sets up a fresh team in a North African capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunis is the capital of Tunisia, and the adjective describes anything from there.

clue.text: Sturdy person like George or David maybe on strike

parts.words: person like George or David maybe
parts.note: George and David are patron saints of England and Wales, ST meaning saint
striking workers are out

explanation.surface: A tough man named George or David is taking industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout means strong and solidly built, as is something sturdy.

clue.text: Odd men out, sirs sadly taken amiss

indicators.note: sadly means poorly or badly, so the letters are arranged badly

explanation.surface: Eccentric men, alas, are offended when called sir.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taken amiss has been wrongly interpreted, so misread or misconstrued.

clue.text: Port boozer knocked back after ten, getting drunk

indicators.note: after places the reversed boozer behind the shuffled number
getting drunk means the letters stagger into a new order
knocked back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a toper is a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: A drinker downs a glass of port after ten o'clock and gets drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the drink; it is a harbour. 'getting drunk' makes ENT from TEN, and 'knocked back' turns TOPER to REPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrepot is a port or trading centre where goods are imported for re-export.

clue.text: Sailor returning home, good sailor

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
in means at home

explanation.surface: A seaman coming home is a fine seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning home' reads as a sailor coming back; 'returning' reverses TAR to RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Royal Navy a rating is a non-commissioned sailor.
